Corpse Cadence Necromancer

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

Untested theorycraft: nobody publishes this build and it has not been played. It exists because four separate 3.1.0 changes all point the same way and no current Necromancer build collects them. Corpse Explosion's Miasma upgrade went from 145% to 210% and Bloody Mess from 50% to 75%; The Gloom Ward now procs every 6th damage instance instead of every 8th; and Red Blessing's maximum Overpower bonus was cut from 4 to 2. In other words this patch paid corpse throughput and taxed Overpower - and the class's meta build is an Overpower build. The hypothesis below asks whether a build that scales on how fast it can make and eat corpses beats one that scales on a stack cap that was just halved. Be clear about what this is not: it is not cross-checked against a tier list, because no tier list ranks it. InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list carries three A-tier Necromancer builds - Full Summon, Blood Lance and Storm Golem - and no S-tier one, which is the same ceiling every other source gives the class; a corpse build is not on anyone's list at all.

Rotation
  1. Gather, detonate, re-seed: Corpse Tendrils on cooldown to pull the pack onto the corpses, Corpse Explosion held down, Sever to reposition and re-seed, and Reap only when Essence is genuinely empty.
  2. Blood Mist when you need to be Unstoppable.
Variants

Leveling — Sever into a pack, which drops a corpse and moves you; Corpse Tendrils to pull the pack onto the corpses; Corpse Explosion until the corpses are gone; Reap to make more. Blood Mist when you need to be Unstoppable, and it eats one more corpse on the way out. What you are watching at this stage is simple: does the ground ever run out of bodies? If it does, the build has failed its first test and no amount of gear fixes it.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and The Gloom Ward in hand. Before that item half the hypothesis is untestable.

Early Endgame — Corpse Tendrils on cooldown to gather, Corpse Explosion held down, Sever to reposition and re-seed corpses, Reap only when Essence is genuinely empty. This is the stage where you collect the number that decides the build: Flesh Eater uptime. Read it off the buff bar over a full Nightmare Dungeon.
Move on when Flesh Eater visibly up more than half the time. If it is not, stop here - the hypothesis has failed and necromancer-meta-blood-wave is a better character.

Late Endgame — Unchanged: gather, detonate, re-seed. What changes is that you should now be measuring rather than playing - single-target damage against a lair boss is the number that decides whether this build goes to the push stage at all.
Move on when You have run the single-target comparison against necromancer-meta-blood-wave and this build is within reach on bosses as well as ahead on packs. If it is not, that is the honest end of the experiment.

Pushing — Untested at push tiers by definition. The predicted failure is boss rooms: one target means one corpse, and one corpse means the cadence this build is named for does not exist. Expect to swap to necromancer-meta-blood-wave for anything boss-heavy, and treat a Pit run here as a measurement rather than a push.

Uniques
  • offhand Necromancer class unique, one-handed shield. Dedicated table: Harbinger of Hatred, in Nahantu near the Kurast Docks waypoint, 1x Greater Lair Key (keys drop from the Initiate lair bosses). This is the item the proc-cadence half of the hypothesis rests on - it now fires every 6th damage instance rather than every 8th - so farm it before you judge the build. Where →
  • gloves Necromancer class unique. Dedicated table: Lord Zir, in The Darkened Way east of Kyovashad, Fractured Peaks, 1x Lair Key (key from the Blood Maiden in Helltide). Taken here on the strength of its 3.1.0 buff from 50-60% to 80-100% and nothing more - the knowledge base records the buff but not the wording of the power, so treat this slot as the first one to re-evaluate once you have read the item in game. Where →
  • amulet General Unique Pool, so any lair boss can drop it, or a Horadric Cube conversion. Chosen over Red Blessing deliberately: Red Blessing's maximum Overpower bonus was cut from 4 to 2 in 3.1.0, which is one of the four facts this build is built on. Where →

Point allocation, in order46 points across 6 nodes

Provenance, stated plainly: this allocation is the game-specialist's, not a published one. No source publishes a skill tree for this build because no source publishes this build - it is an untested hypothesis. The skills and their names come from knowledge/classes/necromancer.md, which is the class-fact authority for the live season, and the point counts are a starting shape to test rather than a measured allocation. Every skill here ranks to 15 in the usual way.

Skill point priority

  1. Corpse Explosion first and hardest, with Miasma - it is the whole build and its upgrade went from 145% to 210% in 3.1.0
  2. Sever next, because it is both mobility and a corpse generator, and corpse supply is the resource this build actually spends
  3. Reap for the second corpse source and for Essence
  4. Corpse Tendrils to group, and because consuming corpses is what activates Flesh Eater
  5. Blood Mist at one point: Unstoppable, plus another corpse eaten
  6. Bone Prison last - it is here for the attack speed, which matters less to a build whose damage is a detonation rather than a swing

Skill point priority

  1. Corpse Explosion maxed with Miasma; every other point is about keeping it fed
  2. Corpse Tendrils maxed - grouping is what turns one detonation into a pack clear, and the consumption is the Flesh Eater trigger
  3. Sever maxed for corpse supply and mobility
  4. Reap kept low once Essence regeneration is on gear
  5. Blood Mist and Bone Prison at one point
  6. Stat shape to aim for, and it is deliberately different from the meta build's: Essence Regeneration matters far less here because Corpse Explosion is paid for in corpses, so the free budget goes to Shadow damage and cooldown reduction on Corpse Tendrils

Board & glyph focus

Route toward Flesh Eater before anything else: its 60% multiplier for consuming corpses is the node the whole hypothesis is about, and unlike the meta build's Bloodbath it does not care about Overpower stacks at all.

Plan

Activity-level, not build-level, and doubly so here: no source publishes War Plan picks for any Necromancer build, and this build has no source at all. The nine picks below are Maxroll's build-agnostic endgame progression priorities with the activity that owns each node named. They are correct for any Season 14 character and specific to none. No `level` is recorded because no source publishes an order.

What is lit9 picks recorded on 5 of 7 activities. Everything else is dimmed, not ruled out: the trees below are the game's own 100 nodes, and a War Plan is per character.
Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

Untested theorycraft: nobody publishes this build and it has not been played. It exists because four separate 3.1.0 changes all point the same way and no current Necromancer build collects them. Corpse Explosion's Miasma upgrade went from 145% to 210% and Bloody Mess from 50% to 75%; The Gloom Ward now procs every 6th damage instance instead of every 8th; and Red Blessing's maximum Overpower bonus was cut from 4 to 2. In other words this patch paid corpse throughput and taxed Overpower - and the class's meta build is an Overpower build. The hypothesis below asks whether a build that scales on how fast it can make and eat corpses beats one that scales on a stack cap that was just halved. Be clear about what this is not: it is not cross-checked against a tier list, because no tier list ranks it. InfinityBuilds' 2026-08-02 list carries three A-tier Necromancer builds - Full Summon, Blood Lance and Storm Golem - and no S-tier one, which is the same ceiling every other source gives the class; a corpse build is not on anyone's list at all.

Rotation
  1. Gather, detonate, re-seed: Corpse Tendrils on cooldown to pull the pack onto the corpses, Corpse Explosion held down, Sever to reposition and re-seed, and Reap only when Essence is genuinely empty.
  2. Blood Mist when you need to be Unstoppable.
Variants

Leveling — Sever into a pack, which drops a corpse and moves you; Corpse Tendrils to pull the pack onto the corpses; Corpse Explosion until the corpses are gone; Reap to make more. Blood Mist when you need to be Unstoppable, and it eats one more corpse on the way out. What you are watching at this stage is simple: does the ground ever run out of bodies? If it does, the build has failed its first test and no amount of gear fixes it.
Move on when Level 70, Torment 1, and The Gloom Ward in hand. Before that item half the hypothesis is untestable.

Early Endgame — Corpse Tendrils on cooldown to gather, Corpse Explosion held down, Sever to reposition and re-seed corpses, Reap only when Essence is genuinely empty. This is the stage where you collect the number that decides the build: Flesh Eater uptime. Read it off the buff bar over a full Nightmare Dungeon.
Move on when Flesh Eater visibly up more than half the time. If it is not, stop here - the hypothesis has failed and necromancer-meta-blood-wave is a better character.

Late Endgame — Unchanged: gather, detonate, re-seed. What changes is that you should now be measuring rather than playing - single-target damage against a lair boss is the number that decides whether this build goes to the push stage at all.
Move on when You have run the single-target comparison against necromancer-meta-blood-wave and this build is within reach on bosses as well as ahead on packs. If it is not, that is the honest end of the experiment.

Pushing — Untested at push tiers by definition. The predicted failure is boss rooms: one target means one corpse, and one corpse means the cadence this build is named for does not exist. Expect to swap to necromancer-meta-blood-wave for anything boss-heavy, and treat a Pit run here as a measurement rather than a push.

Reasoning

HypothesisCorpse throughput is now a better scaling axis for Necromancer than Overpower stacking. Three of the four relevant 3.1.0 changes raise what a corpse is worth (Corpse Explosion Miasma 145% to 210%, Bloody Mess 50% to 75%, The Gloom Ward proc cadence 8th damage instance to 6th) while the fourth halves the Overpower ceiling the meta build is built on (Red Blessing maximum Overpower bonus 4 to 2). If Sever, Reap and Corpse Tendrils together can keep Corpse Explosion permanently fed, the Flesh Eater legendary node's 60% multiplier for consuming corpses fires continuously rather than opportunistically, and the build scales on cadence - casts per second - instead of on a capped stack count.
Confidencemedium
How to test itTest in this order and abandon early if step 2 fails. (1) Measure corpses generated per second with Sever and Reap alone, then with Corpse Tendrils added: the whole build rests on corpse supply and if supply is the bottleneck nothing downstream matters. (2) Watch whether Flesh Eater's 60% multiplier is actually up more than half the time. The meta build triggers it opportunistically with Blood Mist; the claim here is that a corpse build holds it permanently, and that is a claim you can read directly off the buff bar. (3) Check whether The Gloom Ward's every-6th-instance proc keeps pace with Corpse Explosion's own hit count or desynchronises against a small pack - the 8th-to-6th change is the thinnest of the four facts this build rests on and it may simply not matter. (4) Compare Pit clear time against necromancer-meta-blood-wave at equal gear. The prediction is that this wins on packs and loses badly on single targets, because Blood Wave has Kessime's Legacy doubling every cast and a corpse build has no equivalent when there is only one body to explode. If it also loses on packs, the hypothesis is wrong and there is nothing to salvage. (5) Finally, check whether Aspect of Serration's critical strike chance going 5% to 10% is worth a slot at all here: most of the damage is a corpse detonation rather than a weapon hit, and crit may simply be the wrong stat for this build the way it is for the Evade Counterswarm Spiritborn.

Flame Surge

Core skillAldkin

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Fate: Aflame

Basic Attack: Fire Shot

Aldkin channels a cone of flame for 4 seconds, repeatedly dealing 80% Fire damage.

Aldkin's Mercenary Core Skill alters his Fate and Basic Attack.

Aldkin hurls a flaming bolt at an enemy, dealing 90% Fire damage and 55% Burning damage over 4 seconds.

Haunt

Core skillAldkin

Cooldown: 14 seconds

Fate: Forsaken

Basic Attack: Shadow Strike

Aldkin emits 3 ghostly souls at enemies, each Haunting their victims and dealing 90% Shadow damage over 10 seconds. If a target dies while being Haunted, its soul jumps to another target.

Aldkin's Mercenary Core Skill alters his Fate and Basic Attack.

Aldkin shoots a burst of shadow bolts at an enemy, each dealing 30% Shadow damage.

Storm of Fire

Iconic skillAldkin

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Aldkin rains a Fire Storm down from the sky that deals 300% Fire damage on impact and remains on the ground for 10 seconds. Every second, the Fire Storm Burns enemies within for 55% damage over 2.5 seconds.

Enemies hit by Fire Storm's impact or aftershocks have a 30% chance to be Stunned for 1.0 seconds.

Wave of Flame

Iconic skillAldkin

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Aldkin conjures a mass of flames forward, repeatedly dealing 550% Fire damage, Knocking Back enemies, and destroying small missiles.

Field of Languish

Iconic skillAldkin

Cooldown: 20 seconds

Aldkin desiccates an area for 6 seconds, Slowing enemies within by 40% and reducing their damage dealt by 20%.

Chain of Souls

Iconic skillAldkin

Cooldown: 21 seconds

Aldkin chains up to 10 enemies to himself, Tethering to them and dealing 84% Shadow damage over 2.5 seconds.

When the chains expire, they deal 35% Shadow damage and Stun their victims for 2.5 seconds.

Terrify

PassiveAldkin

Hits of Aldkin's Haunt have a 30% chance to inflict Vulnerable on enemies for 4 seconds.

Exhaustion

PassiveAldkin

Aldkin's Shadow damage has a 10% chance to Daze enemies for 2 seconds.

Paranoia

PassiveAldkin

Lucky Hit: Attacks against Languishing enemies have up to a 20% chance to Daze them for 1.0 seconds.

Languishing enemies take 15%[x] increased damage from you.

Condemned

PassiveAldkin

You instantly kill Languishing enemies with less than 40% Life. Does not work on Elites.

Shared Pain

PassiveAldkin

Aldkin's Chain of Souls Cooldown is reduced by 1.5 seconds when a chained target dies.

Amplified Suffering

PassiveAldkin

Damaging a Soul Chained enemy detonates the chain early, dealing 50% Shadow damage around them.

Covered in Ash

PassiveAldkin

Hits of Aldkin's Flame Surge Slow enemies by 20% and deal an additional 60% Burning damage over 3 seconds.

Raging Violence

PassiveAldkin

Allies gain 15%[+] Critical Strike Chance against enemies affected by Flame Surge.

Ember's Gift

PassiveAldkin

You restore 33 Resource per second while inside Aldkin's Fire Storm.

Eradication

PassiveAldkin

Enemies killed within Aldkin's Fire Storm explode for heavy Fire damage.

Raging Havoc

PassiveAldkin

Enemies damaged by Aldkin's Wave of Flame take 15%[x] increased Damage Over Time for 4 seconds.

Burning Chaos

PassiveAldkin

Aldkin's Wave of Flame Cooldown resets when you cast an Ultimate Skill.

Tree of Plenty

Tree of Whispers

The Tree offers a fourth Whisper Cache choice.

Headrotten Feast

Tree of Whispers

Headrotten Bosses that are drawn to Exposed Roots have +1 Monster Power, and will always drop a Whisper Cache.

Resplendent Favor

Tree of Whispers

Each Whisper Cache has a chance to drop a Resplendent Spark.

Malignant Invasion

Tree of Whispers

Varshan can now appear in a Whisper Ambushes.

Slay Varshan to earn the contents of an Ancestral Collection of Chaos .

Grim Retribution

Tree of Whispers

Completing a Whisper has a chance to trigger a Whisper Ambush.

These enemies have a chance to burst out the contents of a Collection of Chaos when slain.

Roots of Power

Tree of Whispers

Enemies that are drawn to Exposed Roots have +1 Monster Power.

Planting Corrupted Roots in Helltides yields double rewards.

Colossal Foe

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Ambushes sometimes include Bosses.

These Bosses will always burst out the contents of a Greater Collection of Chaos when slain.

Simple Gifts

Tree of Whispers

The Tree only offers one Whisper Cache choice that will always be a Material Collection or a Collection of Chaos.

Corrupted Roots

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Caches sometimes contain Corrupted Roots.

Plant Corrupted Roots to grow an Exposed Root. These will attract nearby enemies, and have a chance to grow larger and summon more fearsome enemies.

The regions of Sanctuary each bear different fruit.

Wisdom of Whispers

Tree of Whispers

Gain 50% more Experience Orbs in Whisper Caches.

Fortune or Famine

Tree of Whispers

Whisper Caches from the Tree of Whispers are always at least of Greater Quality... or Junk.

Material Wealth

Tree of Whispers

The Tree now only offers Material Collections.

Grim Mysteries

Tree of Whispers

Collections of Chaos are replaced with Collections of Mysteries.

These caches can drop anything.

Chaotic Favor

Tree of Whispers

Completing a Whisper has a small chance to award a Collection of Chaos.

Branching Pathways

Nightmare Dungeons

When advancing to the next dungeon in a Nightmare Escalation, 2 additional Horadric Portals appear.

Fearless Conviction

Nightmare Dungeons

While in a Nightmare Dungeon, killing Elites and Champions grants you stacks of Conviction.

Getting hit by an Elite or Champion causes you to lose a stack of Conviction.

A Conviction Chest appears at the end of the dungeon that grants rewards for each remaining Conviction. This chest has a higher than normal chance to award Attuned Primordial Dust.

Goblinfall

Nightmare Dungeons

Treasure Goblins have a small chance to drop a Nightmare Sigil with the Treasure Breach affix.

Nemesis

Nightmare Dungeons

Activating a Shrine in a Nightmare Dungeon causes up to 7 Elites to ambush you.

Gauntlet

Nightmare Dungeons

While in a Nightmare Dungeon, slaying an enemy while empowered by a Shrine traps their soul within you.

When the Shrine buff expires, all trapped souls escape and spawn around you as renewed enemies.

Souls will be lost when moving between dungeons in an Escalation Dungeon.

Horadric Hunter

Nightmare Dungeons

Kill 25 Elites across Nightmare Dungeons to reveal a Horadric Altar. Activating it results in one of the following outcomes:

Summon Elites

Summon Treasure Goblins

Summon The Butcher

Gain Riches

Terrible Misfortune

Altar of Avarice

Nightmare Dungeons

Horadric Altars are replaced with Goblin Altars that only summon Treasure Goblins.

Cipher Maps

Nightmare Dungeons

Whenever you would reveal a Horadric Altar, you reveal 2 instead.

Rewarded Faith

Nightmare Dungeons

Gain a random additional buff when claiming a Shrine in a Nightmare Dungeon.

Greed is Good

Nightmare Dungeons

Killing a Treasure Goblin in a Nightmare Dungeon has a small chance to spawn a portal that takes you to the Goblin's Retreat.

Waking Spoils

Nightmare Dungeons

After completing a Nightmare Dungeon, a War's Bounty Chest will spawn that grants additional rewards.

Recurring Nightmare

Nightmare Dungeons

Bosses in Nightmare Dungeons gain +1 Monster Power and have a chance to drop an Escalation Sigil when slain.

Escalation Sigils can only appear in Torment+ difficulty.

Dread Revival

Nightmare Dungeons

Bosses in Nightmare Dungeons have a chance to revive when slain.

Night Terrors

Helltide

You have a chance to be ambushed by Hellborne in Nightmare Dungeons.

Hellborne have a small chance to drop a Profane Mindcage when slain.

Hell's Prize

Helltide

Hell's Prize chests will now appear in Helltide.

These chests offer a massive torrent of items for 666 Aberrant Cinders.

Fall of the Fell

Helltide

Harbingers will emerge from falling meteors twice as often, and drop twice as many Aberrant Cinders when slain.

Harbingers in Helltide have +1 Monster Power.

Meat Brothers

Helltide

Instead of Hellborne, two Butchers that are connected with flaming chains ambush you.

These Butchers each have a high chance to drop a Profane Mindcage when slain.

Hellmouth

Helltide

When a Hellwyrm emerges, it unleashes one of the following:

A Chaos Rift, which releases varied rewards upon collapse.

Maggots, which burst out Experience Orbs when slain.

Bloodseekers, which are more likely to drop Ancestral items when slain.

Wretched Vermin

Helltide

Demonic Rats will frequently attack you in Helltide.

Ashes to Ashes

Helltide

On death, lose all your Aberrant Cinders.

For every 100 Aberrant Cinders you pick up, you gain an additional 10.

Undying Embers

Helltide

You lose no Aberrant Cinders on death.

Infernal Rite

Helltide

Ambushes spawn up to four additional Hellborne.

Hellborne have a higher chance to drop Unique items when slain.

Planar Tremors

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always open a Chaos Rift, and enemies that emerge from it gain +1 Monster Power.

The first time a Chaos Rift opens, there is a chance that another will open.

Tainted Shrines

Helltide

While empowered by a Shrine in Helltide, slain enemies grant double the progress to your Threat Level.

Hated Foe

Helltide

Maximum Threat enemies that ambush you gain +1 Monster Power.

Chaotic Echoes

Helltide

Collapsed Chaos Rifts have a chance to reopen.

Bursting Brood

Helltide

Maggots and Pangs of Duriel explode when killed and will often drop Boss Trophies.

Writhe and Rot

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always spew Maggots that gain +1 Monster Power.

Sometimes, a Pang of Duriel will also crawl forth. Lair Keys often burst out of Pangs of Duriel.

Bound by Blood

Helltide

Bloodseekers are connected with flaming chains.

When slain, Bloodseekers drop items that match the category of the last opened Tortured Gift.

Crimson Scent

Helltide

Hellwyrms will always call forth Bloodseekers that gain +1 Monster Power.

Greater Bloodseekers may also emerge, which have a high chance to drop Legendary items when slain.

Idols of War

The Undercity

Greater Tributes of Armament more frequently drop throughout Sanctuary and have an additional Bargain choices.

Trials and Tributes

The Undercity

For each Portal Prankster you slay within the Undercity, a Tribute Chest appears after killing the District Boss.

Tribute Chests are unlocked by offering a Tribute.

Gutter Filth

The Undercity

When you activate any Beacon within the Undercity, there is a small chance to summon a Portal Prankster.

Invasion Portals will sometimes summon Rats of varying amounts.

Endless Swarm

The Undercity

Invasion Portals now appear in the Undercity.

The enemies that emerge grant Attunement when slain.

Jade Epiphany

The Undercity

When you gain an Attunement level in the Undercity, Experience Orbs appear around you.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Finely Tuned

The Undercity

Gain additional Tuning Prisms when completing the Undercity at maximum Attunement.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Pathfinder

The Undercity

When you reach maximum Attunement, a portal to the final floor of the Undercity appears.

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Unfortunate Souls

The Undercity

Invasion Portals can now summon Wisps that attach to you and vanish if you die.

Each Wisp you save will reward you with Forgotten Souls and other Crafting Materials at the end of the run.

Initiative

The Undercity

When you find the District Boss you gain the Initiative buff, which has a duration equal to your remaining Time. Initiative is lost upon death.

If you slay the District Boss with Initiative active, you receive Tribute rewards as if your Attunement was 2 higher (max 6).

All enemies within the Undercity have +1 Monster Power.

Last Gasp

The Undercity

Time collected from slain enemies with 5 seconds or less remaining in the Undercity doubles the Time earned.

Bauble Day

The Undercity

If you slay a Portal Prankster within the Undercity, the Cabochon Merchant will appear after killing the District Boss.

The Cabochon Merchant will sell you Runes and Gems for Gold.

Lair of Plenty

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses have +1 Monster Power.

Gain +1 Hoard Chest when you slay a Lair Boss (excluding Belial).

Infernal Deception

Lair Bosses

Belial can now ambush you after completing the Infernal Hordes.

Two by Two

Lair Bosses

After opening a Hoard Chest, there is a low chance a Portal will open that will take you to the Nemesis Lair, where you will fight two Initiate Lair Bosses at the same time.

Slaying both will yield great rewards.

You cannot enter a Nemesis Lair from Belial's throne room.

Nemesis Tides

Lair Bosses

Initiate Lair Bosses have a chance to appear instead of Helltide Commanders after Helltide Events.

Killing Lair Bosses in Helltides while earning the Event Mastery grants many random Lair Boss materials.

This only occurs in Torment+ difficulties.

Exotic Armory

Lair Bosses

Hoard Chests drop one additional Unique Item, but it can be for any Class.

Greater Nemesis

Lair Bosses

After completing a Nemesis Lair, there is a chance that a portal will appear that will take you to a Greater Nemesis Lair. Within this heinous place lies two Greater Lair Bosses.

Slaying both bosses will yield great rewards.

Lair of Runes

Lair Bosses

Lair Bosses have +1 Monster Power.

Lair Bosses have a higher chances of dropping specific Runes.

Ultimate Nemesis

Lair Bosses

After defeating all Bosses within the Greater Nemesis Lair, the Call Of Evil will appear. This altar will accept 3 Superior Lair Keys and open a Portal that takes you to the Ultimate Nemesis Lair.

Inside the Ultimate Nemesis Lair, all enemies gain +5 Monster Power. Defeating the Boss Encounter will award you with 10 Hoard Chests worth of Items.

Golden Hoard

Lair Bosses

All equipment that would drop from Hoard Chests are converted to Gold, except for Unique and Mythic items.

Grigoire's Gambit

Lair Bosses

After opening a Tortured Gift in Helltides, there is a chance Grigoire's knights will ambush you.

When killed in Helltide, they may drop Unique Items available from his Hoard Chest.

Duriel's Invasion

Lair Bosses

When summoning the Blood Maiden in Helltides, there is a chance Duriel can be summoned instead.

Killing Duriel in Helltides can now drop Unique Items from his Hoard Chest.

Out of the Cold

Lair Bosses

When fighting a Boss in a Nightmare Dungeon, the Beast in Ice has a chance to appear and attack you.

When this occurs, killing the Nightmare Dungeon Boss has a chance to drop Unique Items from the Beast in Ice's Hoard Chest.

Children of Zir

Lair Bosses

When exploring the Pit, Lord Zir's Bloodseekers can now ambush you.

Killing them in the Pit can now drop Unique Items from his Hoard Chest.

Dog of Astaroth

Lair Bosses

When fighting a Boss in a Nightmare Dungeon, the Amalgam of Rage has a chance to appear and attack you.

Killing the Amalgam of Rage in Nightmare Dungeons can drop Unique Items associated with Astaroth

Embers of Anguish

Lair Bosses

When exploring the Pit, Embers of Anguish can appear. Activating one drops Progress Orbs, and causes Andariel to ambush you at the end of the Pit.

Killing Andariel in the Pit can now drop Unique Items from her Hoard Chest.

Blood of Bartuc

Lair Bosses

The Fell Council in the Infernal Hordes has +1 Monster Power.

After defeating the Fell Council, the Spoils of Greater Equipment may drop Unique Items associated with Bartuc.

Varshan's Vengeance

Lair Bosses

Varshan and his minions can now appear in a Chaos Wave within the Infernal Hordes.

After killing Varshan in the Infernal Hordes, the Spoils of Greater Equipment may drop Unique Items available from his Hoard Chest.

Exalted Council

Infernal Hordes

Bartuc and the Fell Council have +1 Monster Power and drop additional items when slain.

Council Coffers

Infernal Hordes

The Chest of Talismans will appear after defeating either the Fell Council or Bartuc.

Infernal Hoard

Infernal Hordes

Defeating either the Fell Council or Bartuc reveals the Hoard of Greater Equipment, which contains a colossal deluge of equipment and other rewards.

Forged in Flame

Infernal Hordes

Obducite drops instead of Gem Fragments in the Infernal Hordes.

Flawless Find

Infernal Hordes

Gem Fragments drop instead of Obducite in the Infernal Hordes.

Method and Madness

Infernal Hordes

Your Infernal Offerings are more likely to share a category with your previous choice.

Impending Doom

Infernal Hordes

When the current wave has 10 seconds remaining, Aether Events spawn at all locations.

The Black Pact

Infernal Hordes

An ominous altar appears between waves in the Infernal Hordes.

It can be invoked only once, and provides an Infernal Offering that shares a category with your previous choice.

Reign in Hell

Infernal Hordes

An additional Infernal Offering appears each wave.

However, you suppress Chaos Waves from appearing.

Total Chaos

Infernal Hordes

Chaos Waves appear more frequently.

However, one less Infernal Offering appears each wave.

Bedlam

Infernal Hordes

When you enter a Chaos Wave, gain +50 Aether and all enemies in the Infernal Hordes gain +1 Monster Power.

Pulse of Aether

Infernal Hordes

Suppressing a Chaos Wave grants +50 Aether.

All enemies in the Infernal Hordes gain +1 Monster Power.

Cult of Annihilation

Infernal Hordes

Doomsayers appear during the Infernal Hordes.

Doomsayers are dangerous enemies but also drop Aether.

Scale of Tathamet

Infernal Hordes

Once per wave the Scale of Tathamet may appear, a primordial relic that kills all enemies within the Infernal Hordes.

Devil's Deal

Infernal Hordes

At the start of the Infernal Hordes, gain an Infernal Challenge.

Completing the Infernal Challenge will grant +200 Aether.

Choron's Haste

The Pit

The Pit gains the Haste Mastery objective.

When you kill the Guardian gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance for every 5 minutes left on the Timer.

Damned Thieves

The Pit

Orb Thieves have a chance to spawn in The Pit.

Orb Thieves drop an immense amount of Progress Orbs when killed, but leave a trail of Traps in their wake.

Heart of Stone

The Pit

Begin The Pit carrying the Heart of Stone, a fragile relic that is dropped after taking sustained damage and breaks after dropping 10 times.

While you carry it, enemies can drop bonus Progress Orbs.

After slaying the Guardian, Choron's Pedestal appears. Deposit the Heart of Stone within to gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance.

Choron's Blessing

The Pit

Gain +1 Glyph Upgrade Chance for completing The Pit.

Choron's Favor

The Pit

Special events and encounters become more common in higher Difficulty Tiers of The Pit.

Choron's Soul

The Pit

Choron's Soul now spawns with the Awakened Glyphstone.

Choron's Soul will drop 1 Progress Orb per Glyph Upgrade Chance offered.

All Progress Orbs in The Pit now grant Experience.

Choron's Flesh

The Pit

Choron's Flesh now spawns with the Awakened Glyphstone.

Choron's Flesh will allow you to get valuable Equipment by consuming one of your Glyph Upgrade Chances.

Choron's Shortcut

The Pit

Choron's Portal randomly appears in The Pit.

When used, it will send you to the entrance to the next Pit Floor, or become Unstable and summon either an Elite or a Shrine.

Cursed Rituals

The Pit

Different Ritual Sites now spawn in the Pit, and special Materials can spawn in different environments:

Choron's Blood appears in foliage dense regions

Choron's Sweat appears in stony locations

Choron's Tears appears in mystical places

Sacrificing these Materials at Ritual Sites may grant Gold, Materials, Items, and more.

Pit Butcher

The Pit

The Butcher has a chance to appear anywhere in The Pit.

The Butcher is a Guardian and killing him will complete the run.

However, you fail the run if he kills any player.

Cursed Merchant

The Pit

The Cursed Merchant has a chance to appear when completing the Pit.

The Cursed Merchant will sell Equipment for Artificers Stones.

Cursed Offerings

The Pit

Cursed Machines have a chance to appear while exploring the Pit.

Cursed Machines cost Artificers Stones to activate. Activating one will grant you valuable materials and attract vicious enemies.

The more Cursed Machines you find in a single Pit run, the more lucrative the rewards will become.

Choron's Wager

The Pit

Choron's Wager can appear in The Pit.

Activate it with Artificer's Stones to acquire a challenge, which grants a large amount of Artificer's Stones when completed.
